segments.content:
Chapter 127: 0124 Boss Chen Gets Schooled by Casual Gamers (Extra Chapter for Alliance Leader sfqk)

Actually, Xiaonei was already advertising, but it had always been free.

First, to promote *Sanguosha*.

Second, to promote *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty*.

When Li Xunhuan published the book, he naturally returned the favor. Every purchase of *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty* came with two traditional-style *Sanguosha* bookmarks, which included the official *Sanguosha* website and the online store for the physical cards.

In the future, if Xiaonei opened up public registration, *Sanguosha* would also have built-in quests to help with promotion.

The three things promoted one another!

Xiaonei was the least of their worries. As long as two or three users signed up at a university, it would spread like a contamination source. They would automatically invite their classmates to join, spreading like a virus, and the user base would just keep snowballing.

By New Year's Day, Xiaonei already had over 80,000 registered users, a growth rate that surpassed everyone's expectations.

Such rapid growth was actually a bit troubling, because if it continued, it wouldn't even be a month or two before they'd have to spend money on expanding their servers again.

*Sanguosha* also entered a period of rapid expansion.

With traffic driven from Xiaonei and 17173, they also arranged for people to post on forums, blogs, Tieba, and BBS, plus word-of-mouth from offline players. After New Year's Day, the number of registered users exploded.

Consequently, the sales at the *Sanguosha* Taobao store also rose.

The situation was excellent, progressing more smoothly than imaginable.

This was because both Xiaonea and *Sanguosha* were in a unique business, with absolutely no competitors of the same type to be found!

It was as if Sohu's mid-to-high-level management were collectively blind and deaf. Their Alumni Directory was being bled dry of users, yet they continued to ignore Xiaonei. They didn't even bother adding new features to their own product, too lazy to even copy Xiaonei's homework.

So, what was Sohu doing?

First, they launched Sogou Search, busy fighting Baidu for market share.

Second, their mobile MMS business.

Third, exclusively building and promoting the official NBA China website.

Fourth, ramping up efforts for the Sogou Mall, hoping to capture a larger share of the e-commerce market.

These businesses were all very important. Whether Sohu's Alumni Directory lived or died was something no one within the company cared about.

But someone else did!

And that was the founder of Alumni Directory, CEO Chen.

Chen Yizhou was college classmates with Lei Jun, holding a Master's from MIT and a Ph.D. from Stanford's Graduate School of Business.

He founded Alumni Directory in 1999, and after it was acquired by Sohu, he became Sohu's Vice President in 2000. In 2002, he resigned from Sohu, and the Alumni Directory founding team disbanded. CEO Chen then founded Oak Pacific Interactive.

Right now, Chen Yizhou had three main lines of business:

First, building online communities for young people, mainly relying on value-added SMS services for profit.

Second, creating a network download accelerator, competing in the same arena as Xunlei. It was also bloatware, a whole suite of it, extremely difficult to uninstall, and would install its entire family of software on your system.

Third, Mop.

It was while browsing his own Mop site that Chen Yizhou kept seeing posts mentioning Xiaonei.

He went to check out Xiaonei for a few rounds, then logged into the Alumni Directory he had founded. The contrast between the two was immediately clear.

Chen Yizhou made a transpacific call to an old friend in America: "How's Facebook's momentum right now?"

"It's growing very fast," his old friend said. "Several venture capital firms already want to invest, but Peter Thiel isn't satisfied with the valuation. Negotiations could go on for several more months. Are there any similar internet companies in China?"

Chen Yizhou said, "Not sure."

After hanging up the international call, Chen Yizhou had his subordinate gather information on Xiaonei the very next day.

Within half a day, the relevant information was delivered.

"Xiaonei's founder is named Chen Guiliang. A 'left-behind child' from a rural area. Won first prize in the New Concept Composition Competition and was specially admitted to Peking University. Founded Bytedance shortly after starting his freshman year, then launched Xiaonei... The company is an incubation project of Peking University Science Park and has received a low-interest loan of 500,000 RMB... He has another game, *Sanguosha*, which is currently in open beta..."

Chen Yizhou called over his old partner, Zhou Yahui, "Go to Peking University Science Park and see if you can acquire Xiaonei."

"What's the valuation?" Zhou Yahui asked.

Chen Yizhou said, "5 million."

Zhou Yahui's expression was odd. "USD or RMB?"

"RMB," Chen Yizhou said. "If it were 5 million USD, I'd rather just build one myself."

Zhou Yahui said, "I'm afraid he won't sell."

Chen Yizhou said, "A freshman, and from a small town at that. 5 million is an astronomical figure for him. How about this: if he's still not satisfied, raise it to 8 million."

"I'll give it a try," Zhou Yahui said, "but I'm not confident. We should probably prepare to build our own."

What was Chen Guiliang up to?

Final exams!

Peking University's exam week this year was scheduled from December 30th to January 12th (no exams on New Year's Day holiday).

Additionally, some public electives and general education courses had already started their exams from December 23rd.

Chen Guiliang finished all his exams by January 10th.

During this period, he also brought Guo Feng along with Lawyer Zhou Yingzhuo for a trip to the UnionPay Beijing office. They formally signed the agreement, and Guo Feng was left to discuss the technical integration with UnionPay.

The preliminary date was set for the evening of Friday, January 21st, to end the open beta for the online version of *Sanguosha* and officially launch the game's top-up function.

Before that, he had to do a book signing!

The book signing and the publication date for *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty* were set for the beginning of the middle school winter break.

"What are the pre-order numbers on Dangdang?" Chen Guiliang asked over the phone.

Li Xunhuan's voice was excited. "Over 8,000 copies!"

Chen Guiliang said, "A good sign."

Compared to the other timeline, it was still a far cry. Dangnian Mingyue's version had reached 100,000 pre-orders on Dangdang!

But the specific reasons were complex.

After all, this was early 2005. Online shopping and electronic payments were not well-developed. To have over 8,000 pre-orders was already very impressive.

After Professor Wang and Professor Shang agreed to write forewords, Li Xunhuan used the two of them for publicity.

But he felt it wasn't enough, because while they were famous in academia, they were quite unknown to the general public.

So, Li Xunhuan contacted Cao Wenxuan.

Cao Wenxuan agreed to write a foreword very readily. For one, he could use it to boost his own presence, and for another, it was a way of looking out for a Peking University student.

Dangdang used these three professors for promotion. There was academic authority, there was fame, and with Li Xunhuan getting other writers to post on their blogs, it quickly generated huge attention within the circle.

After hanging up, Chen Guiliang started playing *Sanguosha*.

There was another event today, and they had released a limited-time hero card: Zhu Yuanzhang!

Every player who logged into the game received a game announcement:

"Warm congratulations to Mr. Chen Guiliang, the creator of *Sanguosha* and the boss of our company, on the nationwide online and offline release of his work, *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty*, on January 15th. We are specially releasing the event hero card, Zhu Yuanzhang. Complete the event quests to claim it."

"On January 15th, Mr. Chen Guiliang will be at Oriental Plaza in Beijing for a book signing. On January 16th, Mr. Chen Guiliang will be at the main branch of Shanghai Book City for a book signing. Players in these two cities are welcome to come and show your support if you have time. The boss says he thanks you all!"

"Today, Mr. Chen Guiliang will be logging into the game to compete with fellow *Sanguosha* players. Everyone, please go easy on him."

Seeing this game announcement, the players were very excited.

It was like playing *League of Legends* and possibly getting matched with the lead designer.

There were also some uninformed players who asked in the in-game chat: "The boss writes books too? What exactly does this guy do?"

An informed player immediately answered: "He's a freshman at Peking University and has opened two companies."

"Damn, a freshman opened his own companies? His family must be rich, right?"

"He's a 'left-behind child' from the countryside. He started the companies with his manuscript fees and college entrance exam bonuses."

"Awesome!"

Chen Guiliang entered the game and was automatically placed in a room.

Before the match even started, a player typed: "The Chen Guiliang with the golden ID, that's him, right?"
